text: Functional (defect) yield follows Y = exp(-A * D), with A the die area and D the defect density. An 8 cm^2 reticle-scale photonic processor at D = 0.3 per cm^2 yields only about 9%. What architectural response does this motivate?
choices: Increasing the die area to average out defects
Chiplets and redundant/reroutable meshes, rather than betting on one large defect-free die
Switching from silicon to III-V substrates
Running more MPW shuttles to sample lot-to-lot variation
explanation: Yield collapses exponentially with area (exp(-0.3*8) is about 9%), so large monolithic photonic processors are impractical, motivating chiplets and reroutable/redundant meshes. Choice 0 makes yield worse; choice 2 does not address defect density (III-V has its own defects); choice 3 concerns parametric statistics across lots, not functional defect yield of one die.
